text:
Mira: Hey all — planning to onboard Slate-9B v1 into the model-catalog tonight at 22:00 PT. Plan: pin slate9b:1.0 as the new variant, run a 10% canary for 2 hours, then promote if smoke is clean. Need deploy owner, smoke owner, rollback owner, and someone to watch traces/alerts.

Sam: I can own the deploy + rollback. Will do the push at 22:00 PT and keep rollback window open for 30m after canary. @Mira can you confirm rollout policy? :thumbsup:

Mira: thanks @Sam. Rollout policy: canary=10% for 2h, auto-promote only after no errors and p95 latency spike < 20% above baseline. Manual promote if all checks pass. Rollback conditions: error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5m OR p95 > 300ms for 5m.

Lee: PR merged: https://git.internal/redwood/model-catalog/pulls/412 — catalog entry and pin metadata added (slate9b:1.0 -> tag "prod-candidate").

Devin: I’ll run smoke + perf checks. Quick checklist: functional responses for 20 prompts, p95 latency, token throughput, and sample-quality sanity (top-k similarity to baseline). I’ll run smoke after canary ramp and report within 10m.

Devin: smoke command I’ll use (internal):
```bash
# smoke script - runs 20 prompts across canary
./scripts/smoke_canary.sh --model slate9b:1.0 --endpoint https://canary.api.redwood/models/slate9b/predict
```

Ana: I’ll watch the console, traces, and error budget dashboards. Dashboard links: https://console.redwood/dashboards/slate9b-overview and https://console.redwood/alerts. I’ll set a pager if error rate >1%.

Ojas: infra check: dedicated GPU-pool A has capacity headroom for the canary (shard-a3). No autoscale changes needed for 10%. If we need burst >25% we should coordinate with infra oncall.

Mira: quick note on variant: we’re serving quantized q4f16 variant as prod-candidate. Catalog name: slate9b-1.0-q4f16. @Devin make sure smoke includes string-generation edge cases (long context ~2048 tokens).

Devin: noted — will include long context test and KV cache warmup sequences.

Sam: scheduling: I’ll post a deploy window announcement at 21:45 PT in #eng-ml and #eng-oncall. Plan timeline: 21:45 announce, 22:00 start canary, 22:10 verify basic health, 00:00 (approx) decision to promote or rollback.

Mira: For rollback procedure (quick):
1) Re-pin model-catalog route to previous variant with tag slate9b:0.9
2) Abort further rollouts and set canary weight to 0
3) Trigger infra rollback if GPU pool pressure caused failures
4) Open incident channel if automatic metrics cross thresholds or manual rollback occurs

Sam: I’ll run the exact commands during deploy. Copying snippet for pin/rollback: 
```bash
# pin to a variant
redwoodctl catalog pin --route slate --model slate9b:1.0 --weight 10
# rollback
redwoodctl catalog pin --route slate --model slate9b:0.9 --weight 100
```

Lee: catalog already has previous variant metadata and a snapshot if we need to revert. Backups confirmed.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot scheduled a canary deploy for slate9b:1.0 at 2112223600 (22:00 PT). Status: queued.

Ana: small ask — can we set a brief log-level bump for the canary (debug for inference errors) so traces show context? Will revert after canary.

Ojas: ack — can set log-level for shard-a3 for the window. Will revert automatically after 2h.

Devin: one more question — are we using the latency SLO baselines from last week? (was ~140ms p95 for slate-light).

Mira: yes, baseline is the dataset in /evaluations/slate/baseline_2026-03-10. Use that. Thresholds in the rollout doc.

Sam: all set from my side. I’ll post a final checklist at 21:50 and will call rollback if any threshold is hit. Ping me in-thread or @sam.

Mira: awesome — tagging final confirmations: @Sam (deploy/rollback), @Devin (smoke/perf), @Ana (monitoring), @Ojas (infra), @Lee (catalog). Please react with :thumbsup: when ready.

Lee: :thumbsup:
Devin: :thumbsup:
Sam: :thumbsup:
Ana: :thumbsup:
Ojas: :thumbsup:
Mira: great — thanks everyone. I’ll leave the canary params in the rollout doc and post the post-deploy checklist after 22:15.
